_note: EJ keyword rules, shared by news.py and bills.py. Plain rules, no AI. Case-insensitive whole-word match; a trailing * = stem.Seeded with the NJ statute's own vocabulary (N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157) added.
_why_core_terms: These count ALONE -- each is specific enough that it isn't noise (unlike bare 'environment*' or 'pollution', which the research doc flagged as too broad to use unqualified). 'cumulative impact*' and 'overburdened communit*' are the NJ statute's own terms (N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157/161); 'fenceline communit*' is Virginia's.
_why_siting_nouns: Generic by themselves (every warehouse zoning fight uses 'permit'). They only add a tag when a core_term is ALSO present in the same story -- the combination rule the research doc called for, so a bare highway-widening story never counts as EJ on its own. See EJMatcher.match() in src/common.py.
_why_exclude_phrases: Stripped from the text before matching, so a generic development-fee or education-grant story can't be the reason something counts as EJ. None of these appear in core_terms anyway (the research doc's bigger worry -- bare 'environment*' -- is handled by never including it as a core term), but kept as a belt-and-suspenders per the research doc's explicit ask.
nj_statute_cite: N.J.S.A. 13:1D-157 to -161 (NJ's EJ permitting law); NJDEP's overburdened-community definition (35% low-income / 40% minority-or-tribal / 40% limited-English-proficiency census block group) is MEDIUM confidence per the research doc -- not re-verified against the primary NJDEP PDF. Not used as a numeric filter here, only as background.
_why_nj_local_terms: Only for stories whose text names NJ or an NJ place: in-state pollution/siting stories rarely say 'environmental justice' but are exactly what an NJ EJ organizer needs. National stories still need a core EJ term. Added 2026-10-25 after the NJ panel showed only 3 stories in 6 months.
_why_exclude_outlets: Lawyer-ad pages ride on contamination keywords; drop outlets whose name contains these.
